 Judgment
Dated this the 7th day of February, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.1132/2014 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Perumbavoor is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 25.7.2014.

According to the petitioner, on 25.7.2014 at about 1.30 p.m., while he was walking through the side of Chalakudy-Angamaly HH road, a scooter bearing registration No. KL- 8Z-6294 ridden by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner came from behind and hit him down.
As a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the 2025:KER:16682 offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.34,25,000/- limited to Rs.15,00,000/-
4.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A13 and C1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,15,218/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri..A.N.Santhosh, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.
John Joseph Vettikkad, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.

sentences.text: The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
The main contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal at Rs.12,000/-.
According to him, the petitioner was conducting Pandal and decoration work, earning Rs.25,000/- per month,
In order to prove the same he has produced Exhibit A13 series- income tax returns for the years 2013-14, 2014-15 and 2015-16.
Exhibit A13 will go to show that during the year 2014-15, he had a net income of Rs.2,70,000/-.
It also shows that during the said year he had remitted Rs.3,933/- towards income tax.

Therefore, the net annual income for the year 2014-15 after deducting the income tax, will come to Rs.2,66,067/-
(2,70,000-3,933).
if so, the monthly income of the petitioner after deducting the income tax payable will come to Rs.22,172/-.

The Tribunal has limited the monthly income of the petitioner to Rs.12,000/- on the ground that on a perusal of Exhibit A13 series, it is seen that his annual income has not reduced, but only increased.

The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that since the annual income of the petitioner is increased in the succeeding years, the Tribunal was justified in fixing the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.12,000/-.
In this case the fact that the petitioner sustained 20% permanent physical disability is not in dispute.
In the above circumstances, the question whether the income of the petitioner from his Pandal and decoration work is decreased or not, is not a criteria for assessing the loss of disability.
Therefore, I do not find any merits in the above contention raised by the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent.

Accordingly, the monthly income of the petitioner is fixed at Rs.22,172/-.
12.

In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"Lacerated wound over left eyebrow 6x0.5x1 cm and small lacerated wound over occipital region, fracture posterior lateral wall of left maxilliary sinus with hemosimus, fracture lateral wall of left orbit".
13.

As per Exhibit C1 disability certificate issued by the medical board, the petitioner suffered 20%
permanent physical disability.
The Tribunal, has accepted the permanent physical disability of the petitioner as such and it is not under challenge in this appeal.
Hence, I do not find any grounds to disbelieve the same.
Therefore, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is accepted as 20%, as fixed by the Tribunal.
On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 46 years.

Therefore, 25% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 13, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded Rs.48,000/- being the income for 4 months @
Rs.12,000/-.
Since the notional income of the petitioner is re-fixed at Rs.22,172/-, towards loss of earning he is entitled to get a sum of Rs.88,688/- (22172x4months).
16. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.40,0000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.30,000/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
17. The petitioner sustained serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 5 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 2025:KER:16682 'pain and sufferings', is on the lower side and hence it is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
18.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

19. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.10,56,214/- ,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

20.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.10,56,214/- (Rupees Ten lakh Fifty Six Thousand Two Hundred and Fourteen Only), less the amount already 2025:KER:16682 deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
(Enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%).

21. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per Jose vs United India Insurance Company Ltd on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190004242/
